# =============================================================================
# tessera-term: S7C1T / S8C1T (ESC SP F / ESC SP G) and 8-bit C1 controls   (issue #96, wave 9)
# crates/tessera-term/tests/fixtures/c1_spec.txt
#
# Converted from the #96 spec-researcher's tables (spec-96-c1.md, 2026-11-01) with the milestone lead's decisions
# applied. Every expected value comes from the sources below (xterm's source and ctlseqs, DEC's VT510 manual, esctest2,
# vttest, and for the parser the vte 0.15 source that tessera-vt wraps), never from running tessera. Changes against the
# researcher's tables:
#   - DA1 at level 4 and 5 is `?6L;21;22c`: #97 (merged before #96) added 21 from level 4. The researcher's `?64;22c`
#     predates it.
#   - S6/S7: vte dispatches an OSC that CAN or SUB interrupts (osc_spec.txt T25/T26, decision D-CAN), so the 8-bit OSC
#     does too: the title is set. The researcher wrote "no title" (xterm).
#   - S20: a raw 0x9D in 7-bit mode is an ignored control in ground, so the payload after it is printed as text; the
#     researcher described the 7-bit introducer case (`ESC ]` ... 0x9C), which OQ26 in osc_color_spec.txt pins.
#   - R15/R16 (OSC colour replies) wait for #10's colour queries (wave-8 task 10-colors): `#>` lines below.
#   - The esctest `*_8bit` cases that check only the screen (HTS, IND, NEL, RI, S8C1T_CSI, APC, PM, SOS) are E_* rows
#     in esctest_spec.txt; the ones that read a reply (S8C1T_DCS, DECID_8bit) are rows here (R11, C15).
#   - ECMA-48 section numbers are not cited: the researcher quoted them from memory.
#
# DECISIONS (lead, "Lead decisions (2026-11-01)" in the wave-9 plan)
#   D1  8-bit C1 controls are honoured on INPUT only while 8-bit mode is on (S8C1T, or DECSCL Pc 0/2/absent at level
#       >= 2; Terminal::c1_8bit_replies()). A default 7-bit session treats them as today (= xterm in UTF-8 mode, which
#       ignores C1 in UTF-8: charproc.c, every code point 128..159 is CASE_IGNORE).
#   D2  Rule P: in 8-bit mode a C1 code b (a raw byte 0x80..0x9F that is not part of a UTF-8 character, or the UTF-8
#       encoding C2 80..C2 9F) is processed exactly as the two bytes ESC (b - 0x40), in every parser state.
#   D3  Replies use raw single bytes (9b, not c2 9b); a BEL-terminated OSC reply stays BEL-terminated.
#   D5  S8C1T and S7C1T act only at conformance level >= 2; DECSTR keeps the mode, RIS clears it and keeps the level.
#   D6  xterm's level-1 quirk (the byte after an ignored ESC SP G is swallowed) is not copied.
#   D8  Keys, mouse reports, focus reports and paste brackets go through one helper (tessera_term::to_8bit_controls) at
#       the send point; it rewrites a leading ESC [ / ESC O / ESC P / ESC ] and, after ESC P or ESC ], a trailing ESC \.
#   A3  The 0x9C byte of a UTF-8 character inside a DCS payload (c9 9c = U+025C) no longer ends the DCS, in both modes.
#
# SOURCES (fetched 2026-11-01 by the researcher)
#   [CTL] xterm ctlseqs, "C1 (8-Bit) Control Characters", "S7C1T", "S8C1T", "DECSCL": https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html
#   [XT]  xterm source (ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots master): charproc.c unparseputc1 (a reply's C1 byte is ESC (c-0x40)
#         unless control_eight_bits, else the raw byte), unparseseq, CASE_S7C1T/CASE_S8C1T (`vtXX_level >= 2`), DECSCL,
#         RIS (`show_8bit_control(False)`); ptydata.c writePtyData (raw byte, also in UTF-8 mode); VTPrsTbl.c C1 entries
#         (84 IND, 85 NEL, 88 HTS, 8d RI, 8e SS2, 8f SS3, 90 DCS, 96 SPA, 97 EPA, 98 SOS, 9a DECID, 9b CSI, 9c ST, 9d OSC,
#         9e PM, 9f APC, every other C1 aborts with no effect); misc.c DECRQSS `" p` (`;0` when control_eight_bits);
#         input.c (keys: ANSI_CSI / ANSI_SS3), button.c (mouse, focus, bracketed paste through unparseputc1).
#   [DEC] VT510 RM S8C1T.html / S7C1T.html (level 4/7-bit <-> level 4/8-bit; ignored in VT Level 1), DECSCL.html.
#   [VT]  vttest vt220.c tst_S8C1T + esc.c s8c1t(): ESC SP G, CSI 1;1 H, CSI 6 n, expects 9b 31 3b 31 52.
#   [ET]  esctest2 esctest/tests/{hts,ind,nel,ri,s8c1t,decid,pm,apc,sos}.py: escio.CmdChar writes the raw C1 byte while
#         use8BitControls (escoding.to_binary is latin-1), between Write(S8C1T) and Write(S7C1T).
#   [VTE] vte 0.15.0 src/lib.rs: advance_ground executes a lone invalid byte <= 0x9F and dispatches decoded U+0080..U+009F
#         as execute; advance_dcs_passthrough unhooks on any 0x9C byte; advance_osc_string puts every byte >= 0x20 but
#         ESC/BEL/CAN/SUB into the payload; CAN/SUB in an OSC dispatch it (osc_end); SOS/PM/APC ignore every byte but
#         CAN/SUB/ESC.
#
# FORMAT (tests/c1.rs, one table-driven test through common::check_table; every failing id is reported)
#   ### ID               unique row id; the prefix names the group: F (mode switch), R (replies), C (C1 input),
#                        S (strings), K (keys), M (mouse), P (focus and paste).
#   size: RxC            grid size.
#   step: feed <bytes>   `\e` = ESC, `\xNN` one raw byte, `\u{H}` one scalar UTF-8 encoded (`\u{9b}` = c2 9b), `\\`, `\r`,
#                        `\n`, `\t`; `\e G` is ESC SP G (S8C1T), `\e F` ESC SP F (S7C1T). The test runs every row whole,
#                        byte by byte and split in two at every offset of every feed step; the results must agree.
#   reply: <bytes>|none  the exact Request::Reply bytes queued since the previous `reply:` line (or the start),
#                        concatenated; `none` = no reply. `<PV>` = DA2_PV, `<VERSION>` = the crate version.
#   requests: [..]       the other requests since the previous `requests:` line: `SetTitle("..")`; omitted = not checked.
#   c1_8bit: true|false  Terminal::c1_8bit_replies() after the steps (optional).
#   screen: / cursor:    as csi_spec.txt: one `>` line per row, `|` after the cursor's cell; cursor 0-based (row,col).
#   key: <name> [mods]   (K rows) one key press encoded with encode_key in the keyboard modes the steps left; names are
#                        Up, Home, Delete, Tab, Escape, F<n>, Kp5, Char:<c>; mods are ctrl, shift, alt joined by +.
#   mouse: <press|release> <button> <col>,<row>   (M rows) one encode_mouse report, zero-based cell, in the tracking
#                        mode and encoding the steps left.
#   send: <bytes>        (P rows) a sequence the host sends that no encoder in this crate builds (focus, paste brackets).
#   out7: / out8:        the bytes in 7-bit mode (what the encoder returns, or `send:`) and after to_8bit_controls.
#   cite:/note:/source:/flags: documentation.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# F: the S7C1T / S8C1T state machine, observed through the DA1 probe `\e[c` (and DECRQSS `" p` in F17/F18)
#    DA1 at level 4: 7-bit `\e[?64;21;22c`, 8-bit `\x9b?64;21;22c`.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

### F01_s8c1t_switches_replies_to_8bit
size: 24x80
step: feed \e G
step: feed \e[c
reply: \x9b?64;6;9;21;22c
c1_8bit: true
cite: [CTL] S8C1T "send C1 control characters as 8-bit sequences, e.g., its responses to queries"; [XT] unparseputc1; level 4

### F02_s7c1t_undoes_it
size: 24x80
step: feed \e G\e F\e[c
reply: \e[?64;6;9;21;22c
c1_8bit: false
cite: [CTL] S7C1T; [DEC] S7C1T.html

size: 24x80

reply: \e[?64;6;9;21;22c
c1_8bit: false
cite: [DEC] S7C1T from 7-bit "ignores sequence"

### C19_a0_to_bf_are_not_c1
size: 3x10
step: feed \e G\xa0\xbfX

>��X |
>
>
cursor: (0,3)
cite: [VTE] advance_ground: a lone byte above 0x9F is invalid UTF-8 and prints U+FFFD

### C20_utf8_character_with_a_9c_byte_prints
size: 3x10

>Ü |
>
>

### C22_three_byte_character_with_a_9b_byte

>⅛X |
>
>

### C23_raw_csi_after_text

>A|
>

### C25_decscl_switch_applies_in_the_same_read
size: 24x80
step: feed \e[64"p\e[3;5H\x84
cursor: (3,4)
cite: DECSCL without Pc selects 8-bit mode ([CTL] absent Pc = 0); the 0x84 after it in the same read is IND (#96 review: pins the parser asking for the mode after a CSI)

### C26_ris_switch_applies_in_the_same_read
size: 24x80
step: feed \e G\ec\e[3;5H\x84
cursor: (2,4)
cite: [XT] RIS calls show_8bit_control(False): the 0x84 after it in the same read is an ignored 7-bit control (#96 review: pins the parser asking for the mode after an ESC)

### S19_7bit_dcs_utf8_9c_does_not_end_the_dcs

>A |
>
>

flags: decision

### S19b_8bit_dcs_utf8_9c_does_not_end_the_dcs

### S19c_7bit_dcs_lone_9c_still_ends_the_dcs
size: 24x80
step: feed \eP$qm\x9c
reply: \eP1$r0m\e\\
cite: kept: tessera-vt has always ended a DCS on a lone 0x9C byte ([VTE] advance_dcs_passthrough; tessera-vt crate docs "String terminators"); only a 0x9C inside a UTF-8 character stopped doing so
flags: decision

size: 24x80

out7: \e[200~
out8: \x9b200~
cite: [XT] button.c _WriteKey

### P02b_bracketed_paste_end
size: 24x80
send: \e[201~
out7: \e[201~
out8: \x9b201~
note: pasted text is sanitised as before: ESC and every C1 control (U+0080..U+009F) are removed, so a paste cannot end the
      brackets in either mode (a raw 0x9B cannot occur: the text is a Rust string)
